Title: Haze: All schools in Johor, four Selangor districts closed tomorrow, says Fadhlina
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: All schools in Johor and schools under four district education offices in Selangor will be closed tomorrow as the haze situation in the country remains hazardous.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the four district education offices covered the areas of Bangsar Pudu, Hulu Langat, Gombak and Petaling Perdana.
However, she said that schools in Melaka, Penang, Putrajaya, Labuan, Perak, Pahang, Negri Sembilan, Kelantan, Terengganu, Kedah, Perlis, Sabah and Sarawak would remain open.
"For Kuala Lumpur and Selangor, schools under PPDs (district education offices) other than those stated will also operate as usual," she said.
She said state education directors have been told to set up a Haze Monitoring Task Force involving the state education departments and district education offices.
Fadhlina said parents, guardians and teachers were asked to keep updated with the latest information on school operations through the official platforms of the Ministry and related departments.
"Parents and school communities are asked to refer to official notices from the Education Ministry, the state education departments and their respective PPDs for any latest developments," she said.
Earlier, the ministry said in a statement that the
operating status
of schools would be determined based on daily monitoring of Air Pollutant Index (API) readings.

Title: Haze: Johor postpones special school admission test; schools remain shut until Oct 16
Article:
JOHOR BARU: The Special School Admission Assessment (PKSK), scheduled for tomorrow, has been postponed due to the haze, with a new date to be announced by the Johor Education Department.
The
assessment
is used for admission to selected special schools, and the postponement follows the state's extension of school closures until Oct 16 to protect pupils' health and safety.
Johor Education and Information Committee chairman, Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali, said the five-day closure extension was necessary amid deteriorating air quality.
"Our priority remains ensuring the safety and well-being of Johor's children," he said, thanking the public for their concern and feedback.
He said the Year Four Learning Matrix (MPT4) and other affected assessments would also be rescheduled.
Home-based teaching and learning (PdPR) will continue throughout the closure.
Teachers and school staff are allowed to work from home, while officers at the state and district education departments will report for duty as usual.
The department will continue monitoring air pollution index readings and take further action based on developments and directives from the education ministry.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: HRD Corp to support 3 million training opportunities under 2027 Budget
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Human Resource Development Corporation (HRD Corp) will continue to utilise RM3 billion from its levy funds to support three million training opportunities, in line with the government's efforts to strengthen skills development and workforce competitiveness.
The initiative will focus on professional certifications, upskilling aligned with industry needs, and improving the quality of and access to training.
HRD Corp said the measures supported the 13th Malaysia Plan's (13MP) target of having skilled workers make up 35 per cent of the workforce by 2030.
Its chief executive, Datuk Shamir Aziz, said the emphasis on human capital development in the 2027 Budget reflected the importance of strengthening workers' skills to navigate economic changes and evolving industry needs.
He said HRD Corp would continue to focus on industry-relevant training, recognise professional certifications and the strategic utilisation of levy funds to ensure employers' investments in skills development delivered meaningful value to workers and businesses.
"Efforts to upskill and provide reskilling opportunities must continue to be expanded across all segments of society to create more employment and career advancement opportunities, while supporting the development of a more skilled, productive and competitive workforce," he said.
Under the 2027 Budget, RM40 million has been allocated to HRD Corp for the Madani Professional Caregiver Skills initiative, which aims to strengthen the country's care economy by developing a skilled and professional caregiving workforce.
The initiative is expected to benefit up to 8,000 participants, particularly school leavers, Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) graduates, homemakers, jobseekers and unemployed individuals interested in pursuing careers in the care sector.
Funding will cover training costs, attendance allowances and training kits.
Training will cover elderly care, infant and childcare, care for persons with disabilities, postnatal care and community care.
HRD Corp said the initiative aimed to develop a skilled caregiving workforce while creating career pathways in the growing sector.
The agency, under the purview of the Human Resources Ministry, said it would continue working with industries, employers and training providers to ensure skills development met industry needs, benefited the people and supported economic growth.

Title: Haze: Schools in Melaka, Negri, Pahang, Putrajaya to reopen tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) in Melaka, Negri Sembilan, Pahang and Putrajaya, as well as several areas in Kuala Lumpur and Selangor, will resume normal operations tomorrow.
In  KUALA LUMPUR, the Kuala Lumpur Federal Territory Education Department said MOE educational institutions under the Sentul and Keramat District Education Offices (PPDs) would reopen tomorrow, following a decline in Air Pollutant Index (API) readings in the areas for three consecutive days.
"The latest reading was at a moderate level, with an API of 84 recorded at the CA15W Batu Muda station as of 2 pm today. As such, the implementation of Home-Based Teaching and Learning (PdPR) and the Work From Home (WFH) directive for these areas has been terminated," Kuala Lumpur Federal Territory Education Department said in a statement.
However, the department said schools under the Bangsar/Pudu PPD would remain closed until further notice, as air quality remained at an unhealthy level, with an API reading of 152 recorded at the CA16W Cheras station during the same period.
It said that to ensure continuity of teaching and learning, PdPR and the WFH directive for teachers and Implementing Group Staff (AKP) under the Bangsar/Pudu PPD would continue.
In SELANGOR, the Selangor Education Department said all schools under the administration of the Hulu Langat, Gombak and Petaling Perdana PPDs would remain closed based on the latest API readings.
In a statement, the department also said all schools in other districts in the state would operate as usual tomorrow.
"Teachers and parents are advised to follow official updates from the authorities on developments in air quality and relevant school operation directives.
"Further information on school operations and reopening will be announced through the official channels of the MOE and the department," the statement said.
In MELAKA, schools will resume normal operations tomorrow, as air quality readings remained at moderate levels below 100, according to data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) as of 2pm, with Alor Gajah recording 91, Bukit Rambai 94 and Bandaraya Melaka 96.
In NEGERI SEMBILAN, the Negri Sembilan Education Department also said all MOE educational institutions would operate as usual tomorrow based on the latest air quality monitoring.
It also advised students experiencing respiratory symptoms or those in high-risk groups to wear face masks as a precautionary measure.
In PAHANG, the Pahang Education Department also said all schools in the state would operate as usual tomorrow, with the haze situation and API readings being continuously monitored from time to time through the respective PPDs.
In  PUTRAJAYA, the Putrajaya Federal Territory Education Department said all schools under its administration would operate as usual tomorrow, following API readings remaining below the 150 threshold.
According to the department, analysis of API readings showed a consistent decline over the past three days, with the API standing at 70 as of 2 pm today.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fama to add 241 agri-food outlets under 13MP
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Federal Agricultural Marketing Authority (Fama) will expand its agri-food marketing network with 241 new outlets under the 13th Malaysia Plan.
This will be supported by a RM40 million allocation for outlet rejuvenation.
Fama said the initiative aims to strengthen market access for agricultural producers and entrepreneurs while making the distribution and sale of local agri-food products more efficient and attractive to consumers.
Fama senior director of market institutions division Intan Suraya Ibeni Hajar said the rejuvenation programme goes beyond upgrading the physical appearance of its outlets, emphasising building a modern business ecosystem.
"Rejuvenation is not just about making outlets look better.
"More importantly, it is about developing a more modern business ecosystem so that outlets remain relevant, entrepreneurs become more competitive and consumers have better access to agri-food products," she said.
The 241 new outlets will comprise various marketing channels. They include Pasar Tani, Agrobazaar Rakyat, Agrobazaar Kedai Rakyat, Gerai Buah-Buahan Segar and Karavan Tani.
At the same time, Fama plans to upgrade 411 existing outlets to provide a more conducive, organised and consumer-friendly environment.
The agency is also looking to modernise how entrepreneurs conduct business, with greater adoption of cashless transactions, social media and digital platforms to help them reach customers beyond physical outlets.
This is expected to give small and micro entrepreneurs additional channels to promote their products and expand their customer base as consumer purchasing habits increasingly shift towards digital platforms.
The rejuvenation programme also covers the wholesale segment.
Fama is targeting the development of 15 Agrobazaar Rakyat Pemborongan outlets and four outlets within the wholesale ecosystem.
The expansion is intended to strengthen connections between producers, wholesalers, retailers and consumers, creating a more structured marketing chain for agricultural products.
Fama will also conduct 480 promotional and advocacy programmes to increase awareness of its outlets and encourage consumers to purchase locally produced agri-food products.
Beyond physical infrastructure, entrepreneur development will remain a key component.
A total of 32 training and capacity-building programmes have been planned, comprising two entrepreneur conventions, 20 courses and 10 Pasar Tani Student programmes.
"We want young people to see the agri-food sector as an area with entrepreneurial potential.
"With technology, digital marketing and more modern business models, there is considerable room for the younger generation to explore the sector," said Intan Suraya.
Meanwhile, the Agro-Jaja project will benefit 100 hawkers at RTC Kelantan through business image development and equipment support.
The initiative underscores Fama's broader role in food security, where strengthening production must be matched by reliable and accessible marketing channels.

Title: Tax breaks, wage hike headline 2027 Budget surprises: CIMB Securities
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The 2027 Budget has delivered larger-than-expected tax relief and a higher minimum wage, offering support for household spending while raising cost pressures for businesses, said CIMB Securities.
The basic individual tax relief rises from RM9,000 to RM12,000, while tax rates for chargeable income between RM70,001 and RM150,000 will be cut by one percentage point.
CIMB Securities analyst Ivy Ng Lee Fang said the measures could generate annual tax savings of up to RM1,600 for about five million taxpayers, supporting middle-income consumption.
Businesses will also benefit from lower corporate tax rates for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and expanded sales tax recovery for qualifying machinery and production inputs.
The minimum wage will rise 17.6 per cent to RM2,000 a month from June 2027, benefiting more than four million workers. However, MSMEs with annual sales below RM50 million are exempted.
The government's 2027 fiscal deficit target of 3.3 per cent of gross domestic product is also slightly better than the 3.4 per cent forecast, despite the 2026 deficit estimate being revised to 3.6 per cent.
Ng said the budget is "neutral to mildly positive" for Malaysian equities, with higher disposable income and targeted assistance expected to support consumer companies such as 99 Speed Mart Retail Holdings Bhd, Eco-Shop Marketing Bhd, MR D.I.Y. Group (M) Bhd and QL Resources Bhd.
The RM83 billion development expenditure allocation and continued infrastructure investment favour construction players Gamuda Bhd and Malayan Cement Bhd.
Housing incentives and improved connectivity in Johor could benefit UEM Sunrise Bhd and Eco World Development Group Bhd.
Renewable energy and technology companies could gain from extended green investment incentives and semiconductor funding, she said.
Healthcare providers KPJ Healthcare Bhd and IHH Healthcare Bhd may also benefit from opportunities linked to public hospital outsourcing and MediAsas.
Ng said higher minimum wages will increase costs for labour-intensive plantation, glove manufacturing, retail and services businesses, although implementation from June 2027 limits the immediate earnings impact.
Companies that improve productivity through efficiency measures and automation will be better placed to offset higher labour costs.
She said overall, the minimum-wage increase is expected to have a limited direct impact on aggregate FBM KLCI earnings in 2027, while the budget's consumption and investment measures provide selective support for listed companies.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: TH depositors' money not used to fund Perkeso for religious workers - Zulkifli
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Senator Dr Zulkifli Hasan said that Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) depositors' savings were not used to pay Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) contributions for 40,000 mosque personnel and takmir teachers nationwide.
He said a special government allocation fully funded the contributions, channeled through TH as the implementing agency.
Zulkifli said the government's decision to fully fund the contributions recognises religious personnel's service and helps safeguard their welfare, social protection and wellbeing.
"Any claims or assumptions that pilgrims' savings have been used are entirely untrue and speculative," he said in a statement today.
The beneficiaries include imams, bilals, mosque caretakers and takmir teachers serving Muslim communities nationwide.
Zulkifli said the government is committed to ensuring that TH upholds integrity in managing its trust funds and maintains transparent corporate governance in accordance with Syariah principles.
He said the government will continue to prioritise the welfare of mosque personnel and takmir teachers to safeguard religious institutions and support the development of the Muslim community in Malaysia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Negri Sembilan schools to reopen tomorrow as air quality improves
Article:
SEREMBAN: All Education Ministry (MOE) educational institutions in Negri Sembilan will resume normal operations tomorrow following a temporary closure last Friday due to poor air quality.
In a statement today, the Negri Sembilan Education Department said the decision was made after monitoring prevailing weather conditions and the latest Air Pollutant Index (API) readings.
"The department wishes to inform that all MOE educational institutions in Negri Sembilan will operate as usual on Monday, Oct 12 based on the monitoring of current conditions and the latest API readings," the statement read.
However, school administrators have been instructed to continue monitoring air quality, comply with existing guidelines and take the necessary precautions to safeguard the health and safety of pupils and school personnel.
The department also advised pupils to wear face masks as a precaution, particularly those experiencing respiratory symptoms or belonging to high-risk groups.
"The Negri Sembilan Education Department will continue to monitor developments closely and issue official updates should there be any changes. Parents and guardians are advised to rely on official department channels for the latest information," it added.
All schools in Negri Sembilan were ordered to close last Friday after API monitoring stations in Nilai, Seremban and Port Dickson recorded unhealthy air quality levels for three consecutive days.

Title: FIA sees bigger motorsport role for Malaysia beyond F1
Article:
THE successful return to the Formula 1 (F1) spotlight at Sepang has put Malaysia's motorsport credentials back on the global stage and FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem believes the chequered flag should be only the beginning.
Rather than chasing an F1 comeback alone, Malaysia has the ingredients to become a broader motorsport hub, drawing on its established racing culture, passionate fan base and growing pool of enthusiasts, he said.
"Malaysia, to me, is not only about Formula 1. Malaysia, to me, is about motorsport," Ben Sulayem told the New Straits Times and three other media a few hours before the rain-delayed Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia last Sunday.
[[nid:1553175]]
He said the country could look beyond F1 to a wider FIA racing portfolio, including the World Rally Championship, Formula E, World Endurance Championship and cross-country events, while strengthening the grassroots pipeline through karting and rallying.
"You give them karting. You give them cheaper karting. You give them cheaper cross-car. You give them cheaper rally cars. This is the way to go," he said.
Ben Sulayem said the FIA's role is not simply to add more F1 races, but to broaden participation in motorsport and create pathways for enthusiasts and young competitors.
He said Malaysia had already demonstrated that it has a strong motorsport following, with the response to the return of international racing at Sepang showing that interest had remained despite the nine-year absence of F1.
The 65-year-old Emirati was particularly impressed by Malaysian fans and officials during the F1 race weekend, describing them as knowledgeable and passionate.
"The educated fans and the educated staff. You have a very amazing culture," he said.
[[nid:1553174]]
He also praised the cooperation between Malaysian and Bahraini officials, saying the two sides worked together effectively on the ground.
"What really amazed me is the harmonisation between Malaysian and Bahrain. Not at the top level. I'm talking about here on the ground. This is very, very impressive," he said.
For Ben Sulayem, that response demonstrated that Malaysia's motorsport passion had not disappeared during its absence from F1.
"They were there, but they were waiting for an opportunity to show their passion," he said.
He also highlighted the potential for Malaysia and the wider Asia Pacific region to contribute more to the global motorsport ecosystem, pointing to the region's economic strength, manufacturing base and diverse automotive culture.
While F1 remains the sport's biggest global platform, Ben Sulayem said the FIA's broader objective was to grow motorsport across multiple disciplines.
"We have to continue the WRC… There is the World Endurance Championship, Formula E, all of this. And now the cross-country. There is so much," he said.
For Malaysia, that could mean using the renewed attention on Sepang as a springboard for a wider motorsport strategy rather than treating F1 as the sole measure of success.
Ben Sulayem said Malaysia had the ingredients needed to build that future.
"You have a great fan base. You have enthusiasts. You have people who love motorsport. What do you give them?" he asked.
In the end, Sepang's unexpected return could hardly have produced a more compelling advertisement for the circuit, in sporting terms.
The race was delayed by heavy rain, the opening laps were shaped by treacherous conditions and tyre choices, and multiple Safety Car periods repeatedly changed the complexion of the contest.
Max Verstappen eventually emerged as the winner, but the result was far from straightforward.
He lost the lead at the start before recovering it through a combination of pace and strategy, while Kimi Antonelli held second and Lewis Hamilton produced one of the drives of the race to climb from deep in the field to third.
Charles Leclerc also recovered strongly to fourth.
[[nid:1553173]]
That unpredictability played directly into Sepang's strengths. The circuit has long been known for its demanding layout, high tyre degradation and tropical weather, and the 2026 race once again showed how those ingredients can produce genuine strategic and sporting drama.
Just as importantly, Malaysia demonstrated that its nine-year absence had not diminished its ability to stage F1 at the highest level.
The successful organisation of a race brought in at short notice - replacing the cancelled Bahrain event - gave Sepang an opportunity to prove its operational readiness as well as its sporting credentials.
The chequered flag, therefore, may not mark Malaysia's F1 story.
If the country can build on the momentum generated by a memorable race and translate it into a wider motorsport proposition, Sepang's return could prove to be less a one-off encore and more the reopening of a door to the global racing world.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: M'sia condemns deadly attacks in Saudi Arabia, urges peaceful resolution
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has strongly condemned the deadly attacks targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure in Saudi Arabia on Saturday (Oct 10), which claimed lives, left several people injured and disrupted airport operations and commercial flights.
In a statement on Sunday, the Foreign Ministry reaffirmed Malaysia's solidarity with Saudi Arabia and its support for the Kingdom's efforts to safeguard its sovereignty, territorial integrity and national security.
"Malaysia is seriously concerned by the recent escalation of hostilities and violence, and urges all parties to respect international law and pursue a peaceful resolution through dialogue and diplomacy, towards restoring lasting peace, security and stability in the region," the statement read.
The ministry said Malaysia also extended its heartfelt condolences and sympathies over the loss of lives and wished those injured a speedy recovery.
In a statement on Sunday, the Saudi General Authority of Civil Aviation said 12 people were killed and 309 injured in Saturday's attack on the King Khalid International Airport.
Four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshi nationals, and one each from the United States, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Palestine, and Sudan were killed in the attack.
Earlier, Malaysia's Foreign Ministry reported that there were no Malaysian casualties following Saturday's attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and a projectile landing near King Fahd International Airport in Dammam.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US activists deploy poll volunteers over Trump intimidation fears
Article:
US civil rights and pro-democracy groups have begun sending out trained volunteers to counter the possible deployment of armed federal agents to polling locations ahead of next month's midterm elections.
The Vote Safe initiative, launched as early voting began in Ohio this week, accuses President Donald Trump's administration of suppressing turnout by repeatedly raising the possibility of federal intervention around an election that could strip Republicans of control of Congress.
The campaign is putting clergy, veterans, teachers and other community volunteers at voting stations there and later in Georgia, North Carolina and Michigan – four states with closely watched races in November's midterm elections.
Organisers say volunteers will explain voting rights, try to de-escalate confrontations and document potential intimidation or other misconduct.
"The fear is the point, and we must do something about it," Mary Corcoran, executive director of the Save America Movement, told reporters on a press call.
"Left unanswered, fear does the work of keeping people home without a single agent setting foot at a polling place."
Vote Safe brings together Corcoran's organisation, civil rights leader Al Sharpton's National Action Network and the American Federation of Teachers (AFT) union.
Trump has made unsubstantiated warnings of widespread election fraud a centrepiece of his political movement and has pursued restrictions on mail-in voting and proof-of-citizenship requirements, some of which have been blocked by courts.
He has also refused to categorically rule out extraordinary measures around the Nov 3 vote.
Asked in a September interview with Time magazine about declaring a national emergency, Trump said: "I don't rule anything out or in. We'll see."
He also declined to dismiss the possibility of using Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents at voting locations or invoking the Insurrection Act, which allows presidents under certain circumstances to deploy troops domestically.
The administration says it has no plan for a broad ICE presence at polling sites, while the military has assured lawmakers it is not currently intending to deploy troops.
But Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin has said immigration officers could nevertheless appear at a voting location to serve a warrant or respond to a threat.
"I've never seen in the decades I've been involved more fear and apprehension among voters," Sharpton said, describing worries he encountered during a recent visit to Ohio.
The Trump administration has been targeting the state's Haitian community and Sharpton argued that immigration enforcement had generated particular anxiety among African Americans over the possibility of encounters with federal agents confusing them with refugees.
Sharpton says some legal residents he encountered around Cleveland feared being "snatched up and deported."
AFT president Randi Weingarten rejected the administration's argument that a federal presence could be necessary to protect election integrity.
"You do not need ICE at polls to determine whether or not there's fraud," she said. "ICE at polls is about fear."
Trump rejected his 2020 election defeat, making baseless accusations of fraud, and his attempt to overturn the result culminated in the 2021 attack on the US Capitol by his supporters.
This year he has again repeatedly accused Democrats of intending to cheat, while his administration has sought voter records from states and encouraged expanded federal monitoring of elections.
The Justice Department says such monitoring is intended to ensure compliance with voting laws and protect election integrity.
Steve Schmidt, a former Republican strategist who co-founded the Save America Movement, argued that Trump's rhetoric risked undermining acceptance of the November result.
"They have started with the premise that any result they don't like is an illegitimate one," Schmidt told reporters.
Vote Safe organisers stress that their own volunteers will be unarmed and nonpartisan, and say their purpose is not to confront officials but to provide a familiar presence and record what happens.
Sharpton said that mattered because most voters were not hardened political activists.
"They're regular people," he said, "and they just need the comfort of knowing that they're not by themselves."
* The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pahang schools to operate as usual tomorrow despite haze
Article:
KUANTAN: All schools in Pahang will operate as usual tomorrow despite the haze, the Pahang Education Department said.
In a statement today, the department said any changes would be communicated from time to time through the respective district education offices, depending on developments in Air Pollutant Index (API) readings.
"Amid the haze, all teachers, pupils, members of the Implementing Group (AKP) and school staff are encouraged to wear face masks for their safety and health. Ensure that the masks properly cover the nose and mouth.
"Parents, guardians and school staff are advised to follow official announcements from their respective schools.
"The safety, health and welfare of pupils and the education community remain the department's priority," it said.
Last Friday, all educational institutions in Rompin under the Pahang Education Department were temporarily closed until conditions were deemed safe and further instructions were issued.

Title: Firefly cancels Subang-Seletar flights over haze, weather concerns
Article:
SINGAPORE: Firefly has cancelled all scheduled flights between Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport in Subang and Seletar Airport in Singapore from Oct 10 to 12 as a precautionary safety measure due to weather and haze conditions.
In an advisory, the airline said the cancellation involves six daily services: FY3122 and FY3123, FY3124 and FY3125, FY3126 and FY3127, FY3128 and FY3129, FY3130 and FY3131, as well as FY3132 and FY3133.
"Affected passengers are being contacted and reallocated onto available Malaysia Airlines services via the Kuala Lumpur Singapore route, subject to seat availability.
"Passengers who opt not to proceed with the reallocated flights are eligible for a full refund, which will be credited back to the original payment method within 30 working days," the advisory dated Oct 10 said.
The airline said it was also closely monitoring developments amid the evolving weather situation.
Further updates on flight schedules will be communicated directly to affected customers, it added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'They can no longer blame DAP': Loke distances party from MB motion
Article:
SEREMBAN: DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke has denied the party's involvement in any plan to table a no-confidence motion against Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim, saying the party is focused on serving the people.
The Transport Minister said DAP leaders were no longer part of the state administration and were concentrating on their responsibilities outside the government.
"We have never been involved in any such effort (the adat crisis and the no-confidence motion against the MB). As I have stressed before, we only focus on our work and remain committed to the duties entrusted to us by the people.
"I see this ongoing turmoil as having no end, as it involves a complex issue with many aspects, including the Yang di-Pertuan Besar (Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir) and so on.
"This is beyond our duty, and for DAP, we stay focused on our work, which is to serve the people. As for their (Barisan Nasional/Perikatan Nasional) manoeuvres, that is up to them, as they have the majority in the state assembly," he told reporters after the 24th DAP Negri Sembilan Annual Convention here.
Loke was responding to rumours of a no-confidence motion against Ismail at the next state assembly sitting.
https://www.nst.com.my/news/regional/2026/10/1552462/jalaluddin-denies-plans-no-confidence-motion-against-negri-sembilan
Negri Sembilan Umno liaison committee chairman Datuk Jalaluddin Alias has denied any such plan, while Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said he would ensure the motion did not proceed if the claims were true.
Loke said BN and PN had no reason not to continue administering the state as usual, following Tuanku Muhriz's decree that the menteri besar submit the names of new assemblymen to be appointed as executive councillors.
"It should not be a problem for them to choose others as executive councillors, but it is up to their actions.
"Clearly, it is truly strange today that a state government has only a menteri besar and no executive councillors. Of course, the administration cannot run perfectly, as many administrative matters need the approval of the State Executive Council," he said.
He said DAP would not interfere in the matter, even if the party had been blamed during the state election campaign for causing the turmoil.
"Today, we are outside the government and they can no longer blame us. They cannot use DAP as an excuse," he said.
In his speech, Loke urged the party leadership to prepare for an uncertain political situation, including the possibility of another Negri Sembilan election.
"The situation in Negri Sembilan today is very uncertain. Various issues have arisen and there are many problems to be faced. This uncertainty has never happened in the history of our state. So we must always be prepared to strengthen the party," he said.
https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2026/10/1549680/ten-former-negri-sembilan-exco-members-challenge-gazette-revoking
On Wednesday, 10 former Negri Sembilan state executive councillors filed an originating summons at the Seremban High Court challenging the validity of a gazette revoking their appointments.
Tuanku Muhriz revoked their appointments on Sept 20 with immediate effect, citing a breach of their oath of office.
The dispute stems from an April 19 proclamation by four people claiming to be Undang Yang Empat, the territorial chiefs whose votes determine the Yang di-Pertuan Besar, announcing Tuanku Muhriz's removal under Article 10(1)(b) of the Laws of the Constitution of Negri Sembilan 1959.
The former executive councillors issued a statement on Sept 16 affirming that the removal was legitimate.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RM260mil to strengthen disaster preparedness next year
Article:
IPOH: The government will allocate RM260 million to the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) next year to strengthen disaster preparedness, including providing essential equipment for rescue operations.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the allocation would help address equipment shortages among agencies involved in disaster response, including boats, water pumps and water filtration machines.
He said the equipment was crucial not only for rescue operations but also to ensure access to clean water when disasters disrupted water supplies.
"We know that agencies assisting us, including the police, Fire and Rescue Department, Malaysian Armed Forces and Malaysian Civil Defence Force do not have sufficient equipment.
"So, we are helping them purchase the necessary equipment. These are among the proactive measures announced by the Prime Minister," he said.
He was speaking to reporters after launching the 2026 National Preparedness Month at the Ipoh Convention Centre here today.
Also present were Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad and Nadma director-general Datuk Meor Ismail Meor Akim.
He said the government also aimed to increase the number of permanent evacuation centres in every state next year, with priority given to flood-prone areas that frequently experienced disasters and recorded high numbers of evacuees.
He said the government aimed to provide two permanent evacuation centres in each state, although financial constraints remained a challenge in meeting the demand within a short period.
"Our target is two centres for each state, but with the additional allocation next year, we will increase the number according to requirements," he said.
In the 2027 Budget tabled by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on Friday, the government announced RM260 million for Nadma to strengthen the country's disaster preparedness.
The government also agreed to double financial assistance for repairing disaster victims' homes from RM5,000 to RM10,000.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Maybe they don't need our help': Malaysia awaits Indonesia on haze aid
Article:
IPOH: Malaysia is still awaiting a response from Indonesia to its offer of assistance to put out forest fires in Sumatra and Kalimantan, which have contributed to the transboundary haze crisis.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the offer was conveyed directly to Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto and Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka during his recent official visit to Jakarta.
He said Malaysia was prepared to deploy a water-bombing aircraft, three helicopters and 52 personnel to assist firefighting operations in Kalimantan.
"However, there has been no response so far. We are taking a positive view (husnuzon), perhaps they do not require our assistance," he told a press conference after launching National Preparedness Month (BKN) 2026 at the Ipoh Convention Centre here today.
Zahid said the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), together with the Foreign Ministry, had also sent an official letter to its Indonesian counterparts to coordinate the offer of assistance.
On the possibility of Malaysia taking legal action over the transboundary haze issue, he said the matter had been referred to the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) for consideration, if necessary.
However, he said preventive measures and coordination through regional cooperation should take priority over legal action.
"If there is an Asean spirit, preventive measures and coordination to prevent such incidents from happening would be better than legal action," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ahmad Maslan confident Umno will cooperate with Pas in Melaka election
Article:
JASIN: Umno Supreme Council member Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Maslan is confident that Barisan Nasional (BN) will reach a political understanding with Pas for the Melaka state election to advance Muslim unity.
Ahmad, who is also Deputy Works Minister, said he hoped the cooperation would materialise through an agreement between the two parties.
"Negotiations are still ongoing, but I am confident Umno will cooperate with Pas in the Melaka state election. I am very, very confident that efforts to unite the ummah will be realised.
"Let us pray together that this unity can be achieved," he said at a meeting with the BN machinery for the Serkam state constituency in Umbai here today.
Also present were former Jasin MP Datuk Seri Ahmad Hamzah, Jasin Umno deputy division chief Datuk Azman Abdullah and former Serkam assemblyman Datuk Zaidi Attan.
Ahmad also said BN was unlikely to succeed in the state election if it worked with Pakatan Harapan (PH), which he claimed was increasingly being rejected by voters.
"BN is unlikely to succeed if it works with PH, as the coalition has been rejected, beginning in Sabah, followed by Johor and Negri Sembilan. This will be proven in Melaka and Sarawak soon," he said.
Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh was previously reported as saying that BN would use the "BN Plus" formula in the state election, with negotiations with other parties to begin only after the dissolution of the state assembly.
Ab Rauf said BN aimed to defend all 21 state seats it won in the 2021 election, while the seven seats won by other parties would be open for negotiations on possible cooperation.
Meanwhile, Ahmad, who is also BN War Room Secretariat chief, said the 'ABCDEF' formula was among the coalition's key strategies for the election, focusing on its campaign machinery, candidates, data and public sentiment.
He said the formula comprised six elements: continuous activities, a strong campaign machinery, the best candidates, data usage, public sentiment and permitted funding.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kelantan Syariah Court confirms divorce after man stabs wife
Article:
KOTA BARU: The Kelantan Syariah High Court today confirmed a cerai taklik after ruling that a man had breached his conditional divorce pronouncement by stabbing his wife six times on Oct 5.
Judge Mohd Anwan Ab Muttalib made the decision after hearing the 47-year-old man's admission during proceedings that lasted about an hour.
The court found that the defendant had breached Section 50 of the Kelantan Islamic Family Law Enactment 2002, which provides for divorce by taklik or a conditional undertaking made during marriage.
Anwan said the ruling was made on the grounds that the husband had caused physical harm to his wife, in breach of the condition stipulated during their marriage.
"After hearing the defendant's admission, the court today ruled in favour of the plaintiff's claim and confirmed the 'taklik' divorce.
"The court found that the defendant had breached the 'taklik' pronouncement made during their marriage about six years ago by stabbing the plaintiff six times, causing her serious injuries.
"She is currently receiving treatment at Hospital Raja Perempuan Zainab II," the court said.
The 44-year-old plaintiff, who works as a nurse, filed for divorce on Sept 21.
She was represented by lawyer Sufian Zakaria of Hafiz Sufian & Co, while the defendant was unrepresented.
Earlier, the man who was still under remand, arrived at the court about 8.45am clad with a green t-shirt and blue pant.
He has been remanded by the police since Oct 6 to assist in the stabbing incident that happened at Kampung Padang Lepai.
It was reported that a nurse was seriously injured after being
stabbed six times
by her husband at their home in Kampung Padang Lepai.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: South Korea completes trial of Arctic shipping route
Article:
SEOUL: A South Korean container ship returned on Sunday from a trial voyage through the Arctic, testing an alternative route opened by melting sea ice as conflict in the Middle East disrupts global shipping.
The "PanStar Acro" made the round trip to Europe in less time than the conventional route through the Suez Canal, officials said, but the initiative has drawn concerns that increased traffic could accelerate Arctic ice loss.
The Arctic route could also expose operators to sanctions-related risks because it runs along Russia's northern coast.
"The 'PanStar Acro', which embarked on a trial voyage along the Arctic shipping route on August 22, docked at Jaseongdae Pier in Busan Port," the South Korean oceans and fisheries ministry said in a statement to AFP.
The vessel sailed through the Arctic's Northern Sea Route before making port calls at Felixstowe in Britain, Rotterdam in the Netherlands and Gdansk in Poland, and returning via the same route.
President Lee Jae Myung hailed the successful voyage, saying it "shortened the one-way sailing time by 10 days compared with the conventional route via the Suez Canal."
"It also allowed us to gain valuable experience operating a South Korean container ship in polar waters and to collect navigational data," Lee said on X.
The Middle East conflict, sparked by US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February, has roiled global shipping, prompting governments and operators to explore alternative routes.
Environmental advocates, however, warn that expanded commercial shipping along the Northern Sea Route could threaten the fragile Arctic ecosystem.
Major shipping companies, including CMA-CGM, MSC and Hapag-Lloyd, have pledged to avoid Arctic routes, citing environmental concerns.
The Northern Sea Route is generally more accessible during the warmer months, when reduced sea ice makes navigation easier, although ice conditions remain unpredictable and some vessels still require icebreaker assistance.
Without making any reference to the the environmental concerns, Lee said the successful trial mission would help his country "prepare for the era of Arctic shipping routes."
"We will transform Busan and the southeastern region into a 'southern maritime capital region' and ensure that this new sea route becomes a new engine of growth," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mindef eyes idle military land for food security, veterans' welfare
Article:
KOTA TINGGI: The Defence Ministry (Mindef) is looking to utilise undeveloped Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) land to strengthen national food security and improve military veterans' socioeconomic welfare.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the JanaVeteran Programme, in collaboration with Boustead Plantations (BPlant), could help achieve this objective.
"We do not want Mindef land with no allocation or development plans to sit idle. Some plots have gone untouched for 10 to 15 years simply because there are no plans yet.
"So we want BPlant to help the country strengthen food security," he said at a press conference after launching JanaKomuniti at Felda Air Tawar 3 here today.
He said the initiative would create job opportunities and provide income for military veterans, allowing them to remain productive after retirement.
"Every year, 5,000 military personnel retire, so one approach is to introduce any veteran interested in agriculture to the programme," he said.
Khaled said food security must be taken seriously, as supply shortages or rising food costs could escalate into a national security threat.
He said the situation was comparable to haze, which could become a non-traditional security threat if it persisted and spread widely.
He said the JanaVeteran pilot project began with KayTi ginger cultivation at Ladang Telok Sengat here. Under the model, participants are guaranteed a market for their produce, which BPlant will buy.
Meanwhile, Khaled aims to turn the district into the country's main producer of KayTi ginger through BPlant's collaboration under the JanaKomuniti Programme at Felda Air Tawar 3 and Felda Air Tawar 2.
"When this programme succeeds, we will ultimately have a recognisable KayTi ginger product, with Kota Tinggi becoming the nation's food valley through the cultivation of this ginger," he said.
The JanaKomuniti Programme is one of BPlant's corporate social responsibility initiatives, supported by the Kota Tinggi Parliamentary Office, involving a clustered fertigation ginger farming project.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Imran Khan's party's provincial government suspended by Pakistan president
Article:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan's president suspended the government in a province ruled by the party of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan after declaring a state of emergency on Sunday, his office said, stripping its elected administration of its powers.
The decision comes amid a confrontation between Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's government and Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party, which governs northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.
Khan's party has been rallying for several days to pressure the government for his release, threatening to march on the capital Islamabad in coming days.
President Asif Ali Zardari signed Sharif's advice to declare a state of emergency following a federal cabinet decision, his office said in a statement.
The advice said the provincial government had failed to fight Islamist militancy, according to a statement from Sharif's office.
The constitution allows the federal government to take over some or all provincial government functions during an emergency, but the president's office did not specify how the province would be administered.
Zulfikar Bukhari, a close Khan aide and PTI spokesman, called it a "ridiculous decision", saying Khyber Pakhtunkhwa had the country's "only legitimately elected government."
"This will only lead to further bloodshed, instability and collateral damage," he said, adding that there had always been room for talks but the decision showed negotiations were never the government's intention.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rehda asks stamp duty relief for homes up to RM1mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Rehda Malaysia has urged the government to extend stamp duty exemptions to first-time buyers of homes priced up to RM1 million.
Its president Datuk Zaini Yusoff said the proposed measures under the 2027 Budget will ease upfront costs but called for the eligibility threshold to reflect prevailing house prices, particularly in high-cost urban areas.
Under the measures, first-time buyers will receive full stamp duty exemptions on instruments of transfer and loan agreements for properties priced up to RM500,000.
For properties priced up to RM750,000, buyers will receive full exemption on the first RM500,000 and a 50 per cent exemption on the remaining amount.
"We hope the government will continue reviewing the eligibility threshold in line with prevailing house prices and market conditions, including considering an extension of the incentives to properties priced up to RM1 million," Zaini said in a statement.
Rehda said the RM20 billion in housing financing guarantees under Syarikat Jaminan Kredit Perumahan (SJKP) are expected to benefit about 80,000 first-time homebuyers, particularly those with irregular incomes.
It said access to end-financing remained a key challenge for prospective buyers, making the guarantees important in helping them secure housing loans.
The association said the stamp duty exemptions for the rehabilitation of abandoned housing projects, will facilitate the revival of stalled developments and provide relief to affected purchasers.
The government's continued support for affordable housing was also encouraging, with nearly RM1 billion allocated for Rumah Mesra Rakyat and Program Residensi Rakyat.
Other initiatives, including affordable housing developments by Petronas and Bandar Madani Bukit Jalil, will further expand housing opportunities, particularly for lower-income groups, Rehda said.
However, the association cautioned that rising construction material prices, labour expenses and regulatory compliance costs continued to weigh on developers and housing affordability.
Zaini called for a review of charges imposed by federal and state governments, including infrastructure, utility, statutory, regulatory and compliance fees.
"More needs to be done to ensure a more holistic change in housing affordability, such as the review of all related charges imposed by the federal and state governments.
"These costs remain a challenge in developers' efforts in addressing affordability and we reaffirm our commitment to engage with the government and all relevant parties to meet this goal," he said.
Rehda also welcomed the extension of investment tax allowances of up to 100 per cent for qualifying green technology projects and assets until the end of 2030.
The incentives could encourage wider adoption of sustainable practices, particularly among smaller developers.
Meanwhile, property developer Glomac Bhd called for the stamp duty exemptions to cover genuine home upgrades within the specified price brackets, allowing families moving to homes that better suit their needs to benefit.
Group managing director and chief executive officer Datuk Seri FD Iskandar said extending the exemptions to properties priced up to RM1 million will help buyers in higher-cost urban markets such as the Klang Valley and Penang.
He also urged the government to revive the Home Ownership Campaign to help buyers buy homes and facilitate the sale of completed but unsold residential properties.
He said the RM20 billion SJKP financing guarantee was equally important in helping self-employed individuals and those without fixed incomes overcome difficulties securing home loans.
"Rising construction material, labour and compliance costs continue to weigh on the cost of delivering homes.
"We hope that the infrastructure, utility, statutory and regulatory charges imposed by federal and state governments will also be reviewed, as these directly affect how affordably homes can be priced," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Health Ministry to expedite permanent appointments for contract pharmacists
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Health Ministry is committed to expediting the absorption of contract pharmacists into permanent positions through close cooperation with the Finance Ministry and the government.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said that, as of July, 3,545 pharmacists were still serving on contract under the ministry, while another 115 were on the reserve list for permanent appointments.
"The list of those awaiting permanent appointments is still being processed, but I also want to make a commitment to expedite their absorption into permanent positions," he told reporters at a press conference here today.
He was speaking after launching the National Liver Health Initiative Roadmap 2026-2030 in conjunction with Liver Cancer Awareness Month.
The roadmap will focus on screening and risk stratification for fibrosis to facilitate early detection of liver disease at primary healthcare facilities. This will cover both hepatitis-related and non-hepatitis-related causes, including fatty liver disease among high-risk groups with diabetes and obesity, followed by surveillance for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).
Meanwhile, Dzulkefly confirmed that there were no longer any contract nurses in the public healthcare service, with all nurses now offered permanent positions.
"This is part of the ministry's commitment to ensuring that the public nursing service remains competitive, while safeguarding the welfare of its workforce and continuing to develop and strengthen their career prospects.
"Various improvements have been introduced for nurses, including salary scale adjustments under the Public Service Remuneration System (SSPA) and allowances based on eligibility.
"In addition, nurses have been approved for a 42-hour working week, with opportunities for training and promotion, as well as greater flexibility in placement, including transfers through the Mutual Transfer System (P3S)," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: India's 'cockroach' movement founder says PM Modi an 'embarrassment'
Article:
NEW DELHI: The founder of India's online "cockroach" movement said on Sunday Prime Minister Narendra Modi was an "embarrassment" to the country, soon after being released from detention.
"Modi, as PM, is an embarrassment to India," Abhijeet Dipke said in a social media post.
"Never has this country seen a bigger coward and bully," said the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder, who was detained on Saturday before planned protests over electoral roll revisions.
The group said thousands of protesters were detained before Saturday's planned demonstration in New Delhi, the culmination of weeks of opposition mobilisation following allegations of misconduct during a nationwide voter roll revision.
Dipke and two other CJP leaders were detained before they could disembark from their flight after arriving in the capital from Mumbai.
Ratna Singh, the CJP's head lawyer, said in a social media post that Dipke and the others had been released by an executive magistrate's court.
She said they had been released on the condition that they made "no breach of peace for one year".
Dipke, wearing a white shirt, was driven away in a black vehicle soon after walking out of the court, AFP reporters saw.
Authorities mounted a sweeping security operation across the capital on Saturday, detaining thousands to prevent protesters from gathering at Delhi's Jantar Mantar protest site, the CJP and Indian media reports said.
The protest was organised to demand the resignation of the head of the Election Commission of India (ECI) over the nationwide voter-roll revision.
Media reports said the revision resulted in more than 133 million names being removed from electoral lists.
Election authorities say the exercise was aimed at eliminating duplicate, deceased and fraudulent entries.
Critics say the process has disproportionately affected minorities, particularly Muslims, potentially benefiting Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party.
The ECI has rejected allegations of wrongdoing.
Saturday's detentions triggered sharp criticism from opposition leaders, who accused Modi's government of stifling dissent, and others.
In Geneva, the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights called for the immediate and unconditional release of all those "arbitrarily detained" in New Delhi.
Both the CJP and opposition leader Rahul Gandhi have vowed to press ahead with protests despite the crackdown.
Gandhi said his Congress party "... and the youth of the country will once again take to the streets in large numbers" on Monday.
"The more Modi and his government crack down, the more the anger of Gen Z and students will grow," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cell Broadcast System in final phase to deliver disaster alerts to phones
Article:
IPOH: The Cell Broadcast System, a national disaster warning system announced last year, is in its final phase of development, with live testing scheduled for Nov 19.
Developed by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), the system will send disaster alerts directly to mobile phones in affected areas without requiring recipients' phone numbers, SMS services or an internet connection.
It is intended to complement and eventually replace the existing SMS-based disaster warning system, providing faster, more targeted alerts to people in areas at risk.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said timely warnings could give people precious minutes to evacuate and seek shelter before tragedy struck.
"Through this system, warnings can be sent directly to mobile phones in areas at risk without interfering with or accessing personal data," Zahid said.
The system transmits alerts through mobile networks to compatible devices in designated areas. It requires at least one functioning mobile network in the affected area, regardless of the recipient's service provider.
Similar in principle to the United States' Wireless Emergency Alerts (WEA), the system delivers emergency messages directly to compatible mobile phones in affected areas. The US also uses the Emergency Alert System to disseminate warnings through radio and television broadcasts.
Zahid said public awareness and trust in accurate information were essential to the system's effectiveness.
"The system is in its final phase, but the public must be aware of it and know how to use it. One important thing we must understand is that technology is only effective if the public trusts accurate information," he said.
The system is also being developed to accommodate people with visual or hearing disabilities and those who have difficulty reading.
According to the Communications Ministry, it is designed to support alerts through vibrations and audio using accessibility functions on compatible mobile devices, including screen readers and voice output.
These features are intended to help users with accessibility needs receive and understand emergency information. Accessibility, device compatibility and the needs of target groups will be considered during testing and implementation.
The ministry said the system had an advantage during disasters that disrupted telecommunications and internet services because alerts were transmitted directly through mobile networks. However, a complete mobile network outage would prevent alerts from being delivered until service was restored.
A network recovery plan, coordinated with disaster management agencies, service providers and other relevant stakeholders, would support the restoration and reactivation of affected network facilities.
Zahid was speaking at the opening of National Preparedness Month 2026, themed "Madani Preparedness, A Shared Responsibility", at the Ipoh Convention Centre here today.
Also present were Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad and National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) director-general Datuk Meor Ismail Meor Akim.
Zahid said early warnings could give families time to evacuate before floodwaters rose, help senior citizens reach safety and ensure children were moved to safe places.
"That is why early warnings must be delivered on time, be easy to understand and be followed by action. This is why communication is key," he said.
He urged the public to rely on official channels for disaster-related information, warning that unverified reports could undermine response efforts.
He also commended the Fire and Rescue Department, police and Malaysian Armed Forces for their readiness and proactive efforts to assist disaster victims.
Zahid, who is Nadma chairman, said disaster preparedness must be a priority as increasingly unpredictable weather conditions challenged the country's ability to protect lives and property.
Disasters caused RM636.9 million in losses last year, according to the Department of Statistics Malaysia, Zahid said.
Of the total, RM380.2 million involved public assets and infrastructure.
Although the figure was lower than the RM933.4 million recorded in 2024, the impact on affected communities remained significant, particularly for those who lost their homes and livelihoods, he said.
He said disaster preparedness must focus not only on saving lives but also on protecting homes, livelihoods and the country's economic assets.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: #NSTviral: 'GTA-style' chaos as man flees cops, grabs motorcycle in Wangsa Maju [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A man who attempted to flee from a police officer after his pickup truck crashed into a road median in Wangsa Maju was caught on video attempting to escape on a motorcycle before being subdued by the officer and several motorists.
The incident, which occurred at 11.01am, was captured in videos circulated on Threads, showing the man running from the scene before getting into a scuffle with the officer and attempting to flee on a motorcycle.
In the first clip posted by user @tqriz.hykl on Threads, the man was seen dashing away from the policeman and the orange pickup truck, before crashing into a motorcyclist who had got off his motorcycle at an intersection.
The man then ran across the opposing lane into traffic, with the policeman close behind, towards the roadside.
The two got into a tussle again, and the policeman fell over as the man turned around suddenly.
The second clip begins with the man being apprehended at the intersection by the policeman, with the help of motorists.
A motorist is seen kicking the man while he is on the ground. Another motorist stops the first, before a third stomps on the man.
View on Threads
The caption on the video, which garnered 890,000 views and 15,500 likes, reads: "Has GTA(Grand Theft Auto) VI been released?"
Another user, anne_abdullah, posted a different angle in the comments.
It shows the orange pickup being pursued by a police car across the intersection before crashing into the median.
The truck managed to cross onto the median before it became stranded.
A second clip by the same user shows the motorists rushing to help the policeman. One motorist is seen trying to smash a motorcycle helmet into the man.
During the scuffle, the man tried to take one of the motorcycles left behind by the motorists, apparently to escape, but failed. The owner of the motorcycle then stomped on him.
"The incident happened right before my eyes. I was scared but I recorded anyway," the user wrote.
Netizens reacted with a mix of humour and concern.
Several joked about the scene, while others said police personnel needed to keep fit enough to chase suspects, with one saying it was alarming to watch.
Another comment suggested that many riders had been waiting for such a chance to stomp on someone without legal consequences.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: EP Manufacturing, China partner invest RM100mil in Proton fuel tanks plant
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: EP Manufacturing Bhd has partnered with China's Hebei Shichang Auto Parts Co Ltd to invest RM100 million in a new fuel-tank manufacturing facility to supply Proton Holdings Bhd.
The facility, to be located at EP  Manufacturing's hub in Batang Kali, Selangor, will have an annual production capacity of 200,000 plastic fuel tanks.
Deliveries to Proton's Tanjung Malim plant are scheduled to begin in March next year.
The joint venture supports Proton's expansion plans while strengthening Malaysia's local automotive component supply chain and its potential as a regional manufacturing and export hub.
Under an agreement signed on Oct 9, EP Manufacturing will hold a 51 per cent stake in the joint venture company, EP Shichang Automotive Systems Sdn Bhd, while Hebei Shichang will own the remaining 49 per cent.
Hebei Shichang, which is listed on the Beijing Stock Exchange, specialises in the research, development and production of plastic fuel-tank systems.
Its customers include Chinese automotive manufacturers Geely, Chery, BYD, SAIC, FAW, Changan and BAIC.
EP Manufacturing general manager of business development Mohd Seth Sulaiman said the partnership would strengthen the group's capabilities in advanced automotive components as it seeks to move towards higher-value manufacturing.
"As a partner of Proton for nearly 40 years, we are thrilled to witness the success of the Advanced Modular Architecture (AMA) platform rollout.
"Our strategic joint venture with Hebei Shichang will enable us to support Proton as it expands AMA and reaches even greater heights, both locally and internationally," he said.
Mohd Seth said plastic fuel tanks were technically complex components requiring multi-layer construction to meet stringent safety, pressure and performance requirements.
The collaboration will upgrade EP Manufacturing's existing fuel-tank manufacturing capabilities with technology designed to meet the requirements of Proton and Geely for domestic and export markets.
He said the new business could become a significant revenue contributor, similar to EP Manufacturing's automotive seat operations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid wants states to implement Disaster Risk Reduction Policy 2030
Article:
IPOH: States must translate the National Disaster Risk Reduction Policy 2030 into concrete action plans based on local risks, with clear responsibilities and implementation targets.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said this was crucial as the country braced for potential floods during the Northeast Monsoon and prolonged hot and dry weather linked to the risk of El Nino.
Zahid said both scenarios required early preparation and close coordination among government agencies to minimise risks and protect lives.
"I want every state to translate the National Disaster Risk Reduction Policy 2030 into action plans according to local risks, with clear agency responsibilities and implementation targets.
"This policy must genuinely deliver comprehensive protection for the people," he said in his opening speech of National Preparedness Month 2026 at the Ipoh Convention Centre here today.
Also present were Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad and National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) director-general Datuk Meor Ismail Meor Akim.
He said disaster preparedness should begin before calamities struck, with communities and agencies knowing their respective roles when emergencies occurred.
"Disasters can strike anytime, anywhere. All of this requires proper planning and coordination," he said.
Zahid cited floods in Nepal and a cyclone in Sri Lanka as reminders of how quickly disasters could disrupt lives.
He also pointed to minor earthquake reported in areas, including in Gerik, Perak, where such incidents were unexpected, warning against taking even low-magnitude tremors lightly.
"Although the magnitude on the Richter scale was still low, we must never take such incidents lightly," he said.
He said residents in flood-prone areas must know where to evacuate, who would assist them and how aid could reach them if roads were cut off.
In drought-prone areas, water supplies and agricultural needs must be planned well in advance, he added.
Zahid also called for closer coordination among the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry; Energy Transition and Water Transformation Ministry; Housing and Local Government Ministry and Agriculture and Food Security Ministry.
He said the ministries played key roles in weather monitoring, water supply, rescue operations and food production.
Nearly 30,000 volunteers from 45 agencies across 14 states had participated in more than 1,000 relief missions over the past 10 months, he said, commending their contributions and those of the private sector.
However, he stressed that assistance must be coordinated from the outset to ensure it reached those most in need.
Zahid said he had directed every state to establish permanent disaster evacuation centres at selected schools that had
traditionally served as temporary relief centres.
He also said the distribution of Compassionate Cash Assistance had been streamlined, with Nadma directed to disburse the aid to flood victims before they left temporary evacuation centres.
The move, implemented during the previous Northeast Monsoon season, was intended to help victims meet immediate post-flood expenses, including cleaning their homes and household equipment.
"Previously, even three months after floodwaters had receded, victims would return home without having received the assistance.
They would then have to wait another 30 days before receiving it.
"Now, the money is provided while they are still at temporary evacuation centres," he said.
He urged all parties to reduce risks before disasters struck, protect lives during emergencies and help affected communities recover afterwards.
"Preparedness is not merely a reaction, it is a permanent commitment. The lives of our people are too precious for us to prepare only after something has happened," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka schools to reopen tomorrow as haze improves
Article:
MELAKA: All schools in Melaka will reopen tomorrow after being closed for a day due to haze.
Melaka Education Department director Mahfudzah Mohamed Noor said the decision was made following an improvement in air quality, with the latest Air Pollutant Index (API) readings returning to healthy levels.
She said the decision also took into account prevailing conditions, while prioritising the safety and well-being of pupils, teachers and education institution staff.
"All education institution administrators are urged to take the necessary measures to ensure smooth operations and comply with the latest instructions and guidelines issued by the Education Ministry and relevant authorities.
"Parents and guardians are also advised to monitor their children's health and seek immediate medical attention if they experience symptoms related to air pollution," she said in a statement today.
Mahfudzah said the department would communicate any changes to operating instructions for educational institutions through its official channels from time to time.
Last Thursday, it was reported that all schools in Melaka would be closed the following day after the API reading in Bandaraya Melaka reached 171, an unhealthy level.
During the closure, Home-Based Teaching and Learning (PdPR) was implemented to ensure pupils' learning was not disrupted.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Perak schools to resume normal operations tomorrow
Article:
IPOH: Schools in Perak will resume normal operations tomorrow as air pollutant index (API) readings across the state remain below 150.
Perak Education Department director Zulkafli Mohamed Mokhtar said the decision was made following improvements in air quality, with all monitoring stations in the state recording API readings below the unhealthy threshold of 150 as of 2pm today.
"Therefore, all educational institutions under the Education Ministry in Perak will operate as usual from Oct 12," he said in a statement today.
He said the department would continue to monitor API readings in collaboration with district education offices to ensure appropriate measures were taken in accordance with the ministry's guidelines and directives.
Parents and guardians were urged to stay updated on the latest developments, follow official announcements issued by the department and cooperate with schools to safeguard their children's health and safety.
"The safety, health and welfare of students and the entire education community remain our top priority in all measures taken throughout the ongoing haze situation," he said.
On Friday, all Education Ministry schools and educational institutions in Kinta Utara, Kinta Selatan and Kuala Kangsar were ordered to close due to worsening haze.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: Pakatan to unveil candidates on Oct 18, says Anwar’s aide
Article:
ALOR GAJAH, Oct 11 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) will announce its candidates for the Melaka state election on October 18, with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim expected to personally unveil the line-up, said his political secretary Datuk Azman Abidin.
Azman said the venue for the announcement would be announced at a later date.
“The location of the announcement will be announced later,” he told reporters after attending the ‘Jalinan Madani Rider Jelajah Melaka’ programme, which was also attended by Deputy Higher Education Minister Adam Adli Abd Halim, here today.
On speculation that he would contest the Paya Rumput seat in the election, Azman said he would leave the matter to the party leadership.
He said PKR was targeting seven or eight seats in the election, including Machap Jaya and Rembia.
The Election Commission (EC) has set October 31 for nominations, November 10 for early voting and November 14 for polling, following the dissolution of the Melaka State Legislative Assembly on September 23.
In the 2021 Melaka state election, Barisan Nasional (BN) won 21 of the 28 seats, while PH secured five and Perikatan Nasional (PN) two. — Bernama

Title: Haze: Schools in Melaka, N. Sembilan, Pahang, Putrajaya and parts of KL, Selangor to reopen tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — Educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) in Melaka, Negeri Sembilan, Pahang and Putrajaya, as well as several areas in Kuala Lumpur and Selangor, will resume normal operations tomorrow.
In KUALA LUMPUR, the Kuala Lumpur Federal Territory Education Department said MOE educational institutions under the Sentul and Keramat District Education Offices (PPDs) would reopen tomorrow, following a decline in Air Pollutant Index (API) readings in the areas for three consecutive days.
“The latest reading was at a moderate level, with an API of 84 recorded at the CA15W Batu Muda station as of 2pm today. As such, the implementation of Home-Based Teaching and Learning (PdPR) and the Work From Home (WFH) directive for these areas has been terminated,” JPWPKL said in a statement.
However, JPWPKL said schools under the Bangsar/Pudu PPD would remain closed until further notice, as air quality remained at an unhealthy level, with an API reading of 152 recorded at the CA16W Cheras station during the same period.
It said that to ensure continuity of teaching and learning, PdPR and the WFH directive for teachers and Implementing Group Staff (AKP) under the Bangsar/Pudu PPD would continue.
In SELANGOR, the Selangor Education Department (JPNS) said all schools under the administration of the Hulu Langat, Gombak and Petaling Perdana PPDs would remain closed based on the latest API readings.
In a statement, JPNS also said all schools in other districts in the state would operate as usual tomorrow.
“Teachers and parents are advised to follow official updates from the authorities on developments in air quality and relevant school operation directives.
“Further information on school operations and reopening will be announced through the official channels of the MOE and JPNS,” the statement said.
In MELAKA, schools will resume normal operations tomorrow, as air quality readings remained at moderate levels below 100, according to data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) as of 2pm, with Alor Gajah recording 91, Bukit Rambai 94 and Bandaraya Melaka 96.
In NEGERI SEMBILAN, the Negeri Sembilan Education Department also said all MOE educational institutions would operate as usual tomorrow based on the latest air quality monitoring.
It also advised students experiencing respiratory symptoms or those in high-risk groups to wear face masks as a precautionary measure.
In PAHANG, the Pahang Education Department also said all schools in the state would operate as usual tomorrow, with the haze situation and API readings being continuously monitored from time to time through the respective PPDs.
In PUTRAJAYA, the Putrajaya Federal Territory Education Department (JPWPP) said all schools under its administration would operate as usual tomorrow, following API readings remaining below the 150 threshold.
According to JPWPP, analysis of API readings showed a consistent decline over the past three days, with the API standing at 70 as of 2pm today. — Bernama

Title: Haze: Air quality in Kuching, Miri improves to moderate levels, says DOE
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 11 — Air quality in Kuching and Miri has improved but remains in the moderate category, according to the Department of Environment’s (DOE) Air Pollutant Index of Malaysia (APIMS) portal on Sunday.
Kuching’s Air Pollutant Index (API) reading last recorded an unhealthy level at 2am today, at 111, before dropping to 99 at 3am.
The reading subsequently declined from 153 at 3pm yesterday (Oct 10) to 85 at 3pm today, placing Kuching in the moderate category.
In Miri, the API reading last recorded an unhealthy level at noon today, at 104, before falling to 99 at 1pm.
Miri’s API reading had remained in the moderate category from 3pm yesterday until 11am today, when it rose to 101 before reaching 104 at noon.
As of 3pm today, all air quality monitoring stations in Sarawak recorded API readings within the moderate category.
The readings were Limbang (84), ILP Miri (80), Miri (98), Samalaju (96), Bintulu (94), Mukah (79), Kapit (66), Sibu (87), Sarikei (84), Sri Aman (61), Samarahan (74), Kuching (85) and IPD Serian (70). — The Borneo Post

Title: Digital tools, AI can preserve Dusun language for future generations, says Sabah deputy CM
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 11 — Digital technology, including artificial intelligence (AI), has the potential to become a crucial medium in efforts to preserve the Dusun language, ensuring that this community’s heritage continues to be learned, used, and inherited by future generations.
Sabah Deputy Chief Minister I Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam said that modern technology can be leveraged through the development of digital dictionaries, recordings of Dusun speech, podcast production, and the creation of online learning materials.
He noted that these efforts need to be strengthened through the involvement of the younger generation, educational institutions, and local communities so that the Dusun language remains relevant and continues to be used in daily life.
“When a language is used less and less, we are actually at risk of losing a part of our own community’s identity and heritage,” he said.
“The question is, in the next 50 years, will our children and grandchildren still be able to speak their mother tongue and understand the history, customs, and culture that form the foundation of their identity?” he said in a statement today.
Joachim, who is also Sabah’s Minister of Works and Utilities, made these remarks while speaking at the closing ceremony of the Ranau Dusun Language and Culture Festival in Ranau yesterday.
